skills.name: Durability
skills.summary: The tank.
skills.quiet: You're still standing. Of course you are.
skills.notices: That beam would hold your weight. Probably. It's held worse than you.

ep.speaker: Sanchez of the Burning Bridge
quote: Yeah, I take hits for a living. Men these days are weak one way or another, and I mostly make my money off the ones who are weak in the heart.
ep.intro: Durability is your metabolism and circulation; what commoners call "being in good shape." Who cares if you can shoot fire from your palms when you can inhale the fireball they just threw and breathe it back in their faces?
ep.effect: more HP per level-up, Critical Damage reduction; gates endurance equipment.
ep.high: you look like a pro wrestler and weaker folk start trembling. Not sure they'll dare talk to a walking marble statue, though.
ep.good: gym rats, tomboys, brawlers who tank for the team.
ep.bad: scholars, exam crammers, light-armour fans.

perks.name: Bulwark
perks.t1: Allies directly behind you, in line with the attacker, take 25% less damage from ranged attacks.
perks.t2: 50% less, covering two tiles behind you.

perks.name: Shrug It Off
perks.t1: 2 AP, remove one Body Debuff from yourself.
perks.t2: 1 AP, and gain a shield worth 10% of your max HP.

mastered.name: Last Wall
mastered.flavour: The wall doesn't fall. The wall decides when it's done.
mastered.text: Once per combat, an attack that would drop you to 0 HP leaves you at 1 HP instead, and you take no damage until the start of your next turn.

combos.name: Siege Engine
combos.text: Shove and Break cost 1 AP less, and nothing can knock you back.
combos.deed: Break through a wall to win a fight.

skills.name: Pain Threshold
skills.summary: Wounds don't slow you down.
skills.quiet: Something stung you a while back. Nothing to worry about. Probably.
skills.notices: The burn on your hand is real. You'll want to look at it later.

ep.speaker: Sazmin of the Adamantile Brigade
quote: Want to test if your poison's strong enough? Coat a blade and go poke Knight Jiren in the arm. No, I'm serious. Once he sleepwalked into the snake pen, slept there all night and walked out with a dozen Crobar still hanging off his back. THEN HE WENT AND MADE BREAKFAST. Sometimes I wonder if anyone around here is still normal.
ep.intro: Pain Threshold is why you can take an arrow and still get up. Or change a lightbulb without flipping the breaker? Who knows. Just remember: not feeling pain doesn't mean you can't die. Don't get delusional.
ep.effect: Elemental Damage reduction; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: the "threshold" part disappears and you go numb to anything that hurts. And again: A KNIFE YOU CAN'T FEEL CAN STILL STOP YOUR HEART.
ep.good: bushido duellists the sneaky types keep poisoning, people who hate pain, the last survivor of a house fire, masochists.
ep.bad: anyone who still likes their limbs and doesn't want to lose one because they "forgot fire is hot."

perks.name: Used to the Pain
perks.t1: The first time you're hit each combat, if it took less than 20% of your max HP, +2 AP next turn; if more, −1 AP.
perks.t2: The threshold becomes 30%, the gain +3 AP, and the penalty is gone.

perks.name: Scar Tissue
perks.t1: Each wound you take in a combat adds 5% Elemental Damage reduction for the rest of it, up to 25%.
perks.t2: Up to 40%, and the same stacks apply to limb damage.

mastered.name: Walking Wounded
mastered.flavour: Hurt is information. You've read it all before.
mastered.text: Injuries never cost you AP or Movement. Below half your max HP, you get +1 AP at the start of each turn (the AP ceiling still applies).

combos.name: Bite the Bullet
combos.text: Once per combat, when you would drop to 0 HP, take one more full turn first. You drop at the end of it unless you've been healed above 0 by then.
combos.deed: Fight through an entire combat below a quarter of your max HP.

skills.name: Sensory
skills.summary: Touch, smell, temperature and the ground under your feet. Not sight or sound; that's Vigilant.
skills.quiet: Rain's coming. You can feel it in the knuckles.
skills.notices: The floor is warmer by the far wall. Something runs behind it.

ep.speaker: Sister March of the Lumeri Church
quote: She can feel it, trust me. Even a single sigh. Back when her eyes still worked and her legs hadn't given out, Grandma Marry was already the Grandma Marry she is now. What I always admired most was how she could read the temperature of the air with one finger raised to the sky. Or the way she sits in her deck chair, eyes closed, smelling the morning, with a smile on her lips. Sometimes she makes a twenty-year-old girl like me jealous.
ep.intro: Sensory is how sensitive your skin and senses are to the world: a cold breeze, a scent you can't name, a faint tremor underground. With high Sensory it feels like nature itself is shaking your hand.
ep.effect: Heal/Shield received bonus; unlocks sensation options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: you become one with every movement around you, a little too well. If your ears are that sharp, stay away from concerts. Those speakers don't hit gently.
ep.good: people who stroll for the breeze, travellers who go somewhere just to breathe it, scouts and rogues listening for footsteps.
ep.bad: death metal fans, people who can't take the cold, elves of every kind.

perks.name: Wind on the Skin
perks.t1: When combat starts, learn where one hidden enemy within your Vision Range is.
perks.t2: Every hidden enemy within your Vision Range.

perks.name: Bedside Manner
perks.t1: Touch someone during a conversation (a handshake, a hand on the shoulder) and learn whether their next statement is a lie.
perks.t2: Also learn whether they're afraid, and of whom.

mastered.name: Skin Map
mastered.flavour: The air moves around them. The floor remembers their weight. You don't need eyes.
mastered.text: You always know where every creature within 6 tiles is, hidden or not. Darkness, smoke and invisibility hide nothing inside that range from you.

combos.name: Sixth Sense
combos.text: Hidden enemies within 3 tiles of you are revealed to you and your whole squad.
combos.deed: Catch someone tailing the squad before they strike.

skills.name: Raw Power
skills.summary: Hit harder, bend further, lift higher.
skills.quiet: Your arms are the cleverest thing about you, and that's fine.
skills.notices: The hinges are weaker than the door. Hit those.

ep.speaker: Knight Andre "Giant Fist" of the Adamantile Brigade
quote: Back in the army they kept saying my arms were bigger than my brain. Yeah, maybe. Maybe. If I pulled my brain out and measured it with a ruler, my arm probably is bigger. But you can't arm-wrestle with a brain, and when it comes to arm-wrestling I'm the best there is. So I used my arms to wrestle their brains, and a few concrete tables. Nobody said anything after that.
ep.intro: Just saying the name makes you feel the strength rising. Raw Power isn't technique, calm or authority. It's STRENGTH: hit harder, bend further, lift higher. Things only muscle can do.
ep.effect: Physical Damage and Counter Roll; gates strength equipment.
ep.high: you break locks, doors and bones, and laugh at people who can't. But that much muscle makes it easy to hurt the things you never meant to.
ep.good: martial artists, berserkers, competitive lifters, guys going for the record on the bar's punching machine.
ep.bad: mages, cat and bunny lovers, high nobility who don't want to be called thugs.

perks.name: Breaching Strike
perks.t1: 3 AP, a melee hit that knocks the target back 1 tile.
perks.t2: 2 tiles; a target slammed into a wall takes +50% damage.

perks.name: Grapple
perks.t1: 2 AP, grab an adjacent enemy. It can't move, and attacks anyone but you at −2.
perks.t2: Attacks aimed at you have a 50% chance to hit your captive instead.

mastered.name: Earthbreaker
mastered.flavour: They took cover. You took the cover.
mastered.text: Once per combat, 4 AP: strike the ground in reach. Every creature in the 3×3 around the point of impact takes your melee damage and is knocked Prone, and all cover in that area is destroyed.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 4 AP · Once per combat

combos.name: Siege Engine
combos.text: Shove and Break cost 1 AP less, and nothing can knock you back.
combos.deed: Break through a wall to win a fight.

skills.name: Guts
skills.summary: Fear doesn't get a vote.
skills.quiet: Hold your breath. Walk in. That's the whole secret.
skills.notices: The others are scared of the noise, not the room. The room is quiet.

ep.speaker: Ragoul the Keeper
quote: Why has no one else uncovered the secret of Arganzaz? Because they are a pack of faint hearts, that's why. I saw a jade-inlaid door twenty yards wide slowly opening. I heard a thousand wandering ghosts wailing and smelled ten thousand walking corpses. What they did was scream and run. What I did was hold my breath and walk in. That is why they now call me the Keeper of the secret of Arganzaz.
ep.intro: Guts is your tolerance for anything spooky or scary: a door with a skull over it, or a pitch-black hole with a sign saying "Hole of Pain." What it is doesn't matter. What matters is that you're not scared of it.
ep.effect: Body Debuff save; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you feel like an impregnable fortress. But people don't label things "dangerous" for fun, and you not being scared doesn't stop it from chewing your bones.
ep.good: thrill-seekers, manly men, manly women, holo-streamers filming viral reels in abandoned graveyards.
ep.bad: horror-movie fans, delicate ladies, team leaders and scouts.

perks.name: Into the Dark
perks.t1: Your first move into an unexplored room or area costs 0 AP.
perks.t2: +1 AP on your first turn inside a place that causes Fear.

perks.name: Iron Stomach
perks.t1: Nausea and Fear last at most 1 round on you.
perks.t2: You're immune to both.

mastered.name: Nothing Left to Fear
mastered.flavour: You've already met the worst thing. It blinked first.
mastered.text: You're immune to Fear. Allies within 3 tiles who can see you can't be made Afraid either.

combos.name: Bite the Bullet
combos.text: Once per combat, when you would drop to 0 HP, take one more full turn first. You drop at the end of it unless you've been healed above 0 by then.
combos.deed: Fight through an entire combat below a quarter of your max HP.

skills.name: Intimidation
skills.summary: You run the conversation through fear.
skills.quiet: Manners first. Then the bones.
skills.notices: He keeps touching his collar. He's already afraid; you only have to agree with him.

ep.speaker: Tommy Avencio, the "Papa" of the Smetanita Conjunction
quote: Have you ever had the pleasure of tasting animal marrow? Oh, who am I kidding. A merchant from Mandestra must have tasted every pleasure under the sun. Forgive my peasant manners. And you know what, Mr. Galon? If the shipment I'm waiting for doesn't arrive on time, then with these two peasant hands I'll treat you to a very special marrow broth, made from the bones of your arm. Understand? Snap that dainty hand of yours like a chicken neck, and then we savour that faintly sweet flavour together, like business partners sharing a milkshake. Slurp. Slurp. Slurp.
ep.intro: Intimidation is your control over the fear of whoever stands in front of you. One piercing look, one commanding cough: the person running this conversation is you.
ep.effect: Body Debuff DS bonus; unlocks threat options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: everyone sees a demon in human skin, whether you want it or not. Whether that's good or bad is up to you.
ep.good: people done with smooth talkers' bullshit, people who want every conversation to open with the other guy's trousers turning brown, serial killers.
ep.bad: upstanding middle-class citizens, anyone keeping an angelic image, heartbreakers.

perks.name: Grim Reaper
perks.t1: −1 AP on your first turn of each combat. Each time you KO or kill an enemy on your turn, +2 AP, once per turn.
perks.t2: No first-turn penalty, and every enemy who sees the kill saves against Fear.

perks.name: Bone Talk
perks.t1: Threaten someone with one specific, physical detail and they must answer one question or take a Heart debuff (Shaken).
perks.t2: Works on a group; the leader answers for all of them.

mastered.name: The Name They Whisper
mastered.flavour: They tell stories about you to keep their recruits in line.
mastered.text: When combat starts, every enemy who knows who you are saves against Fear. An enemy at half HP or less that can see you, and fails a Heart save at the end of its turn, surrenders.

combos.name: Charge!
combos.text: Once per turn, a charge of 3 or more tiles straight at an enemy costs no movement AP.
combos.deed: Open a fight by charging the enemy line, and win it.

combos.name: Make Way
combos.text: Moving past enemies never triggers their reactions, and crowds part for you.
combos.deed: Walk through a hostile crowd with no weapon drawn.

skills.name: Athletics
skills.summary: Armour just slows you down.
skills.quiet: Light on your feet. They swing like Orks; you move like you.
skills.notices: There's a ledge under the window. Two steps and you're out of their line.

ep.speaker: Dominik Edelgard, the "Banner Lord" of the 237th Hellraiser Division
quote: Armour? What armour? Oh, I left the vest at base. First-floor locker room, locker 16, key's under the red flowerpot if you want it. Natalia still grumbles every time I deploy: 'Are those two banners on your back for a burial shroud or what?' But the armoury boys lean on tech way too much. What I'm fighting out here are Orks. ORKS. They swing junk machetes, and the gunners aren't any better, aiming with both eyes open. If you can dodge everything they throw at you, armour just slows you down!
ep.intro: Athletics is how nimble and supple you are. It decides how well you pull off anything that needs flexibility: flips, swimming, dodging.
ep.effect: Dodge Roll and Critical Damage; gates agility equipment.
ep.high: your body is light as a feather and limber as a cat. Until someone ties you down. Then you aren't a person who lost a leg, you're a bird that lost its wings. Prepare for the trauma.
ep.good: gymnasts, dancers, guys who spam crouch after every kill.
ep.bad: slow-living types, high nobility, heavy-armour users.

perks.name: Wall Run
perks.t1: As part of a move, run along a wall or across a gap of up to 2 tiles.
perks.t2: Up to 4 tiles, and you can attack mid-run.

perks.name: Roll With It
perks.t1: After a successful dodge, move 1 tile for free.
perks.t2: 2 tiles, and your next attack that turn gets +10% Critical Damage.

mastered.name: Never There
mastered.flavour: Aim where they'll be. They won't be there either.
mastered.text: Your first move each turn provokes no reactions, and ranged attacks against you take −4 while you're moving.

combos.name: Charge!
combos.text: Once per turn, a charge of 3 or more tiles straight at an enemy costs no movement AP.
combos.deed: Open a fight by charging the enemy line, and win it.

combos.name: Dance of Iron
combos.text: After each successful dodge, fire one shot at the attacker for 0 AP.
combos.deed: Dodge three attacks in one round.

skills.name: Dexterity
skills.summary: The gun hand. Reloads, recoil, quick-draw, throws. Attack skill for guns, bows and thrown weapons.
skills.quiet: Breathe. Count the rounds. You have four.
skills.notices: His holster's cut for a left-hand draw. Watch the left.

ep.speaker: Ambrosius Costeau, the Old Drifter
quote: No tricks here. I don't even need to open my eyes. I've carried this revolver since the years before Operation Daggerfall, stranger. Call me old-fashioned, call me outdated, but don't take this old body lightly in a gunfight. Wander within 500 metres and if your head doesn't vanish, your hat will need a big patch. These eyes aren't what they were, but these hands have never left the gunbelt. Identify. Squeeze. Breathe the powder smoke. Dig the grave.
ep.intro: Dexterity measures how reliable you are at anything that needs precision. Anyone can reload a gun or throw a dart. Nobody does it as fast or as clean as you.
ep.effect: throwing range; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: your hands work like a machine and your trained skills fire almost on their own. So you want to use them even when it's the wrong moment, and announcing your habits to the whole world is never a good idea.
ep.good: gunslingers, snipers, blade masters, point strikers.
ep.bad: gamblers, magic users, anyone who doesn't want to be called "hands faster than brain."

perks.name: Origami Hands
perks.t1: 2 AP, build an improvised tool or trap from scraps: a tripwire, a lockpick, a sling.
perks.t2: 1 AP, and your traps deal +50% damage.

perks.name: Running Reload
perks.t1: Reload as part of a move, once per turn.
perks.t2: Clear a jam as part of a move too.

mastered.name: Trick Shot
mastered.flavour: Off the pipe, off the plate, into the second one. You called it.
mastered.text: Once per turn, a ranged attack can ricochet: it ignores cover, and if it hits, a second enemy within 2 tiles of the target takes half the damage.

combos.name: Dance of Iron
combos.text: After each successful dodge, fire one shot at the attacker for 0 AP.
combos.deed: Dodge three attacks in one round.

skills.name: Reaction Speed
skills.summary: Spotting danger is one thing. Moving in time is another.
skills.quiet: You're fast. Fast isn't the same as right.
skills.notices: Glint on the rooftop. Left. Now.

ep.speaker: Yukimura of the Black Scavengers
quote: I shoot first. Honestly, you don't need fancy gear out here. Want it harder? Hand me a couple of daggers. Surviving the lowlands is tough because it has the one thing the desert doesn't: dead buildings. Wherever you go in here, you're swimming through a concrete forest. If they poke out of some dark corner and you don't react in time, a hundred percent you end up strung on a pole. Me, I just throw a knife and duck before they pull the trigger.
ep.intro: Reaction Speed is the time between your eyes firing and your body moving: a glint from an enemy scope, or a strange blink from a partner right before the handshake. Spotting danger is one thing. Reacting in time is another.
ep.effect: Ambush Damage reduction; unlocks reaction options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: you're frighteningly fast and never caught flat-footed. But reacting that fast makes you look plainly impatient, and plenty of times reacting fast just makes things go wrong faster.
ep.good: gamers, sailors, gunners, every other kind of -er, gamblers.
ep.bad: calm people, people who need to save face, anyone who doesn't want to look like they're on speed.

perks.name: Rounding Up
perks.t1: Fractional AP rounds up, not down.
perks.t2: Once per combat, carry 1 unspent AP into your next turn.

perks.name: Catch
perks.t1: Once per round, catch a grenade or thrown weapon aimed at you or an adjacent ally, and throw it back for 1 AP.
perks.t2: The throw back costs 0 AP.

mastered.name: Before the Blink
mastered.flavour: Initiative is a polite word for who was faster. That was you.
mastered.text: You always act first in round 1, whatever the initiative roll, and you get a second reaction each round.

combos.name: Between Heartbeats
combos.text: Once per combat, when an enemy starts an action in your sight, take a 2 AP action first.
combos.deed: Come through an ambush without being hit.

skills.name: Ingenuity
skills.summary: Stealth, sleight of hand, sticky fingers.
skills.quiet: Nobody is watching the back stairs. Nobody ever is.
skills.notices: The guard's keys are on the left hip, and he's tired.

ep.speaker: Lin Shin Long
quote: A thousand gold for two rocks. The number of people still paying in gold coins outside Central City is baffling. Back when I worked the city, I'd swipe a bank card out of some guy's pocket and that was dinner sorted. Back then I still had Travis to crack the cards... People call it petty theft, but the trade takes real skill. First you learn to walk in step with the crowd and spot which pocket bulges most. Then you work out how much weight to slip back in so they don't notice the coins have flown. If you don't know how, don't mess around. The old men at the guard post started carrying shock batons last week, and it hurts like you wouldn't believe.
ep.intro: Ingenuity is the finesse in everything you do: staying unseen while sneaking, picking pockets, that sort of thing.
ep.effect: reduces Ambush Range, raises Ambush Damage; gates finesse equipment.
ep.high: you turn into a cosplayer of the sneaking-soldier legend, flickering in and out of the shadows. But all that shifty behaviour makes it hard to look a cop in the eye.
ep.good: rogues, scouts, bandits, gamblers.
ep.bad: model citizens, uniformed (not undercover) cops, anyone trying to romance a uniformed (not undercover) cop.

perks.name: Sleight of Hand
perks.t1: 2 AP, plant an item (a grenade, a tracker, evidence) on an adjacent target without being seen.
perks.t2: 1 AP, and you can do it mid-conversation.

perks.name: Shadow Step
perks.t1: Moving from cover to cover while in stealth costs half the normal Movement.
perks.t2: After an attack from stealth, roll Ingenuity to stay hidden.

mastered.name: Vanishing Act
mastered.flavour: Everyone saw you. Nobody can say where you went.
mastered.text: Once per combat, 2 AP: drop out of sight wherever you are, even in plain view. You stay hidden until you attack or someone touches you.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 2 AP · Once per combat

combos.name: Just the Repairman
combos.text: When you're spotted sneaking inside an enemy's sight, 50% chance they take you for maintenance staff, as long as you're carrying a toolbox.
combos.deed: Talk your way past a guard who caught you somewhere you shouldn't be.

combos.name: Silent Partner
combos.text: An ally next to you shares your stealth.
combos.deed: Get the whole squad through a guarded area unseen.

combos.name: Dead Signal
combos.text: While in stealth, disable one electronic device within 3 tiles for 1 AP, silently.
combos.deed: Shut down a security system without anyone noticing.

skills.name: Proficiency
skills.summary: The mechanic. Fixes guns, gear and machines in the field, robot squadmates included.
skills.quiet: Every piece fits somewhere. You just have to see all of them.
skills.notices: That turret's feed is jammed on the third link. It's firing half as often as it should.

ep.speaker: Demitri Kortev of Kortev Utility Shack
quote: Yes, yes, a watchmaker and a gunsmith aren't far apart. Lay every part of a pendulum clock on the table and odds are your brain starts shorting out. Guns are the same: picking one up and shooting is a world away from stripping every screw and putting it back. Anyone can read a clock, but how many can fix one? What you need is someone who sees every piece of the puzzle and joins them into one. Like me! Unless you use a digital clock or one of those toy guns from the carnival stalls, in which case: scram. Shoo, shoo.
ep.intro: Proficiency is your grasp of complex mechanisms, from something as small as a stopwatch to something as huge as a transcontinental cannon. All of it can be taken apart by you.
ep.effect: Sigil Draw Core reduction; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you see how everything works, man-made or not. That helps with a lot, but you lose interest in anything that isn't screws and gears, and it cuts you off from human society.
ep.good: engineers, roboticists, weapon modders, clockmakers.
ep.bad: enchanters, magic users, party people, therapists.

perks.name: Jury-Rig
perks.t1: A broken weapon or device works one more time before it fails for good.
perks.t2: Field Repair works at double strength on vehicles and drones.

perks.name: Hot-Swap
perks.t1: Swapping a weapon or a mod costs 0 AP, once per turn.
perks.t2: Twice per turn.

mastered.name: Overhaul
mastered.flavour: It left the factory good. It leaves your bench better.
mastered.text: Field Repair costs 1 AP and restores twice as much. At a long rest, give one weapon or device a permanent extra mod slot (once per item).

combos.name: Field Surgeon
combos.text: Field Repair heals living allies as well as machines, and your heals on robotic allies work at full power.
combos.deed: Bring a squadmate back from below 10% HP.

combos.name: Dead Signal
combos.text: While in stealth, disable one electronic device within 3 tiles for 1 AP, silently.
combos.deed: Shut down a security system without anyone noticing.

skills.name: Vigilant
skills.summary: Sight, sound and hostile intent.
skills.quiet: Your spine went cold a second ago. Listen to it.
skills.notices: Two men in the doorway; one is pretending to drink.

ep.speaker: Vermilion Jasmine of Rigaz Trade Company (RTC™®)
quote: They keep saying I can dodge bullets. As if any human could. They've got a few knives in the neck before they can pull the trigger, that's all. Run enough jobs for old Rourigaz and you'll get used to it: every time someone aims at you, even from the dark, your spine goes cold. Just remember to cut their spine out in return, as a thank-you gift.
ep.intro: Vigilant is the survival instinct your ancestors handed down. An enemy in the bushes, a prying gaze in the dark: with eyes and ears tuned to detail, you notice what's off before anyone else.
ep.effect: Detection Range; unlocks alertness options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: you're hyper-aware of everything you see and hear and can sense danger in a heartbeat. But that alert, you're never sure if the danger is real or you're just imagining things.
ep.good: debtors on the run from loan sharks, husbands afraid of wives in high heels, grunts terrified of punji traps, snipers.
ep.bad: anyone who doesn't want to be called jumpy or a coward.

perks.name: Got You in My Sight
perks.t1: When you see an enemy enter stealth or leave your sight, +2 AP this round; when a sneak attack hits you, −2 AP.
perks.t2: No penalty, and the squad always knows that enemy's last position.

perks.name: Eyes in the Back
perks.t1: You can't be flanked: half cover next to you, and a carried shield's frontal cover, count against a ranged attack from any direction.
perks.t2: Allies next to you can't be flanked either.

mastered.name: Nothing Gets Past
mastered.flavour: You held the line of sight. All of it.
mastered.text: Your Overwatch doesn't stop at the first enemy: every enemy that moves into your line before your next turn draws a shot, as long as you held the AP for it. Each shot hits before the enemy's move finishes.

combos.name: Sixth Sense
combos.text: Hidden enemies within 3 tiles of you are revealed to you and your whole squad.
combos.deed: Catch someone tailing the squad before they strike.

skills.name: Brain Power
skills.summary: Raw processing speed for Sigils. Attack skill for Sigils that strike.
skills.quiet: Breathe. Draw the path in your head first. Then the hand.
skills.notices: The sigil burned blue, not white: a CONDENSE was drawn twice. Someone here is sloppy.

ep.speaker: Professor Avdol of the Science Team
quote: Stop flailing and concentrate. In nearly twenty years of using an Evoker I have never needed to dance a single kata to trigger a sigil. If you want martial arts in your magic, kindly go south and join a sect. I may be a spellcaster, but I am a scientist and they are philosophers. Now breathe deep, memorise the sigil's path, draw it, and press the blue button on the right-hand grip. If you burn through your MagiCore before finishing a Fireball, I'm done teaching you.
ep.intro: Brain Power is your brain's processing speed. In PC-parts terms, it's the difference between two graphics cards. It lets you handle information faster than others, and helps a lot with Sigils and Evokers.
ep.effect: Sigil Damage and Sigil Stay Duration; gates big-brain equipment.
ep.high: your brain is always hunting detail, almost hyperactive. Look at a rock and instead of "where's it from" and "why is it here", you're on "its chemical composition" and "a hundred ways to arrange rocks into a code." Training a brain that big isn't always smart.
ep.good: Evoker users, scientists, researchers.
ep.bad: Emanator users, healers, melee fighters.

perks.name: Hold the Stroke
perks.t1: 1 more of your glyphs can stand on the ground at once before the oldest fades.
perks.t2: 2 extra.

perks.name: Parallel Thought
perks.t1: While one of your Sigils is still active (a field, trap or turret of yours stands), your next Sigil costs 1 AP less.
perks.t2: 2 AP less.

mastered.name: Clean Draw
mastered.flavour: No charge, no smoke, no Flux. Just the shape, perfectly.
mastered.text: Once per combat, draw a Sigil of any length you can draw (up to 4 glyphs) with no Core charge and no Flux.

combos.name: Spoon-Feed
combos.text: 2 AP, explain an enemy's weakness so simply that every ally who hears it gets +2 on attacks against that enemy this round.
combos.deed: Teach someone a Sigil.

skills.name: Rumination
skills.summary: The scientist's library. Mirrors Lore Master.
skills.quiet: You have read about this. Page forty, or thereabouts.
skills.notices: That banner is from the second Daggerfall levy. Those units were disbanded for mutiny.

ep.speaker: Thalatûl the Librarian
quote: The knowledge you need to become a Keeper of Books? Seven hundred and forty-five reigns. Two hundred thousand years of history. Five hundred and forty thousand inventions, great and small. Nine million three hundred and fifty thousand species of plant and animal, and hundreds of millions of pages turned. Now kindly erase your presence from my library.
ep.intro: Rumination is how well you absorb and retain scientific knowledge: history, politics, maths, physics, chemistry. It also lets you look at an object and pull up the theory behind it.
ep.effect: Sigil Range bonus; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you always side with science, experiment and hard data. Great in a lab; uncomfortable with anything science can't explain, like incantations, charms, souls or spiritual links.
ep.good: bookworms, hackermen, tech professionals of every field.
ep.bad: lifters who only care about strength, students of the surreal, the devout, conspiracy preachers on the pirate bands.

perks.name: Footnote
perks.t1: Once per scene, cite a fact; allies who act on it get +1 on that roll.

perks.name: Lab Coat
perks.t1: +3 on saves against chemicals, gases and drugs you've identified.
perks.t2: 2 AP, neutralise one of them for the allies around you.

mastered.name: Established Fact
mastered.flavour: You checked. It's true now.
mastered.text: Once per session, state a fact about the technology, biology or history in the scene. The Narrator makes it true, unless it contradicts something already shown.

combos.name: Spoon-Feed
combos.text: 2 AP, explain an enemy's weakness so simply that every ally who hears it gets +2 on attacks against that enemy this round.
combos.deed: Teach someone a Sigil.

skills.name: Eloquence
skills.summary: Logic as a weapon.
skills.quiet: There is only one truth, and you happen to be holding it.
skills.notices: She said 'before the fire'; the fire was after. She's lying about when.

ep.speaker: Xander Badman of Monsieur Saul's Law Firm
quote: Fine, if you insist, I'll review all the evidence. Aaaand there's nothing worth reviewing. The dashcam at 11:45 shows, plain as day, the defendant stabbing a man to death. And I'm sick of your take-the-punch-take-the-bribe attitude, Your Honour, and your jury's too. The evidence is right there, so why no arrest? Because the defendant comes from a good family? Or because the pile of cash under the table is just too hard to pass up? You know what? As counsel for the plaintiff, I'm going to walk outside and tell the world I won. There is only one truth, and if you disagree it's because you're a pack of nitpicking self-servers. I WIN. BYE-BYE. CLOSE THE COURT.
ep.intro: Eloquence is your power to argue and debate logically, whether you're stuck in a battle of wits or a high courtroom. Believe in yourself, pick apart every word out of your opponent's mouth, cook up something clever and fire it back with confidence.
ep.effect: Brain Debuff DS bonus; unlocks rhetoric options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: you must win EVERY conversation, and you'll use every trick there is, whether the other side meant harm or not. Good or bad? Depends.
ep.good: lawyers, preachers, politicians, keyboard warriors.
ep.bad: quiet types, people who hate arguing, people who'd rather argue with their fists.

perks.name: Overruled!
perks.t1: +2 AP for as long as a Left Brain Debuff you inflicted lasts on an enemy; −2 AP while you carry one yourself.
perks.t2: Works with Right Brain Debuffs too, and your own penalty is halved.

perks.name: Burden of Proof
perks.t1: When an NPC accuses you or the squad, demand evidence. If they can't produce it, they lose the argument outright.
perks.t2: Everyone watching shifts one step toward your side.

mastered.name: Closing Argument
mastered.flavour: You didn't win the argument. You ended it.
mastered.text: Once per scene, make your closing argument. Every NPC listening who isn't ruled by fear or faith accepts its logic, even if they hate where it leads. They can still refuse to act on it.

combos.name: Just the Repairman
combos.text: When you're spotted sneaking inside an enemy's sight, 50% chance they take you for maintenance staff, as long as you're carrying a toolbox.
combos.deed: Talk your way past a guard who caught you somewhere you shouldn't be.

combos.name: Spoon-Feed
combos.text: 2 AP, explain an enemy's weakness so simply that every ally who hears it gets +2 on attacks against that enemy this round.
combos.deed: Teach someone a Sigil.

combos.name: Fire Sermon
combos.text: While you preach (2 AP), your Blessings also leave enemies in range Shaken.
combos.deed: Convert an enemy mid-fight.

skills.name: Visualization
skills.summary: Shapes thought into images and Sigils into forms.
skills.quiet: Thousand-autumn red. You'll never mix it. Try anyway.
skills.notices: The scorch marks fan out from the left. The blast came from the corner, not the door.

ep.speaker: Rémy Étienne, the Second Broom-Bearer
quote: Thinking it in your head is not enough! Master Sakamoto once spent four months mixing just 200 grams of watercolour. He called it 'Thousand-Autumn Red.' And if you must know: I've watched the video of him mixing it over a thousand times, and I still can't make that colour. No one can guess what you might do with a few rose stems, glue and an egg yolk. I wonder what 'Afternoon of Blood' looked like inside his mind. But the undeniable truth is that the way he carried that thought from his head onto paper is irresistible. A beauty only he could paint.
ep.intro: Visualization is your power to picture the world: to take the shapeless thoughts in your head and express them outward as images.
ep.effect: Sigil Range bonus and Elemental Damage; gates image-making equipment.
ep.high: you see the story behind every landscape and make landscapes out of every story. You risk sinking into faraway worlds and forgetting this one.
ep.good: critics, painters, Projector Gear® users.
ep.bad: the near-sighted, people who'd rather feel than describe.

perks.name: Mirage
perks.t1: 2 AP, project a false wall, figure or sound onto a tile in range. Enemies who fail an Analysis check treat it as real for a round.
perks.t2: Two projections, lasting 2 rounds.

perks.name: Blueprint
perks.t1: Sketch the ground before an assault; allies who saw the sketch get +1 Movement in the first round.
perks.t2: And +1 AP.

mastered.name: Solid Image
mastered.flavour: If you imagine it hard enough, it has edges.
mastered.text: Once per combat, one of your projections becomes real for a round: a wall blocks movement and shots, a figure can take one hit meant for an ally.

combos.name: What Could Be
combos.text: Once per session, before a major decision, the Narrator shows you a brief vision of the best outcome within reach, and one way to get there.
combos.deed: Talk someone out of a terrible choice by showing them where it leads.

skills.name: Analysis
skills.summary: Detective work and target analysis. Analyze (2 AP) reveals one enemy's HP, armour, resistances and weak points.
skills.quiet: Send the apology letter later. Find the spy now.
skills.notices: First: no casings. Second: the wall is dented from the far side. He wasn't shot.

ep.speaker: D12.9.6 of the CCEC (Central City Espionage Commission)
quote: Look at the crime scene again. First: this man was never shot. He may be stuck to a wall full of bullet holes, but bullets didn't kill him. Why? Pick up a casing and look closely. Not an enhanced round; nobody is crazy enough to load enhanced rounds into an SMG. It smells of Outburst mana, a foreign Outburst to be exact. Second: the body stayed stuck to the wall until we pulled it off. Some strong force pushed him from the opposite side, and it wasn't an enhanced round. One .700 Blackpoint? Maybe. Fifty .32 Decrkm? Definitely not. From the mana, the victim was hit by an Outburst. The casings and holes say the killer wanted us to believe he died to bullets, enhanced rounds specifically. Send the apology letter. We need to find a spy from Bazaim.
ep.intro: Analysis is your ability to break the world down: work through any situation logically and land on the most correct answer.
ep.effect: Analyze Range; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you over-analyse everything until your view narrows to a slit. Once you pick a detail, your brain glues itself to it and forgets a case usually has more than one.
ep.good: detectives, hunters, assassins, secret agents.
ep.bad: Orks, Rockmen, barbarians.

perks.name: Detective's Eye
perks.t1: In any scene, the Narrator tells you one detail that's out of place.
perks.t2: Two details, and whether they're connected.

perks.name: Pattern Lock
perks.t1: +2 Dodge against any attack you've already seen this combat.
perks.t2: +4, and allies get +2.

mastered.name: Case Closed
mastered.flavour: Everything about them, in the order it matters.
mastered.text: Analyze reveals everything at once: HP, armour, resistances, weak points and what the target wants. Allies attacking an enemy you've analyzed get +2 to hit and +20% damage.

combos.name: Cold Read
combos.text: One Analyze action on an NPC reveals what they want most.
combos.deed: Close a case with a confession.

skills.name: Charisma
skills.summary: Warmth, persuasion, and lying with a smile.
skills.quiet: A gentleman never passes up a conversation he's sure to win.
skills.notices: He wants to be asked, not ordered. Ask him about his ship; he loves it.

ep.speaker: Damian Nox, SuperUltraHyperExclusive Producer for Sibugar Entertainment
quote: I asked whether he'd like a glass of water or anything. Honestly, officers, that afternoon was the first time I'd met Mr. Duboi, and everything in my statement is true. Granted, keeping an electric chair in one's office isn't for everyone, but I'm a lover of the arts. I adore bold, satirical work; how could I not display one of the masterpieces of my collection? It was a regrettable accident. That chair was never used until Mr. Duboi volunteered himself into it. How was I to know he would switch the power on himself and die so needlessly? Tell the court I'll be there. A gentleman like me never passes up a conversation he is certain to win.
ep.intro: Charisma is the power of words: how well you persuade and steer a conversation, and how warm you come across while doing it. Extremely handy for lying and making things up.
ep.effect: Brain Debuff save roll; unlocks persuasion options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: you can talk anyone into anything, but all that warmth makes some people see you as a spineless bootlicker. Depends who you're talking to.
ep.good: politicians, merchants, lawyers.
ep.bad: antiheroes, the antisocial, anyone who hates looking soft in a conversation.

perks.name: Talks Broke Down
perks.t1: In a fight that started because your squad won a dialogue check, +2 AP for the whole fight; in one started by a failed check, −2 AP.
perks.t2: No penalty, and one enemy hesitates (−1 AP) in round 1.

perks.name: Crowd Pleaser
perks.t1: Talking to a crowd, make one roll for the whole crowd, at +2.
perks.t2: You can turn the crowd against one named person.

mastered.name: Everyone's Friend
mastered.flavour: You've known them for ten minutes. They'd lend you their car.
mastered.text: Once per scene, one NPC who doesn't already hate you treats you as a trusted friend until the scene ends. They share what a friend would, and your first lie to them always lands.

combos.name: Make Way
combos.text: Moving past enemies never triggers their reactions, and crowds part for you.
combos.deed: Walk through a hostile crowd with no weapon drawn.

skills.name: Empathy
skills.summary: Feeling what the other side feels, enemies included.
skills.quiet: What was he thinking, right before? You'll wonder for years.
skills.notices: She isn't angry at you. She's terrified for the boy in the back.

ep.speaker: Paul Remarque
quote: I'd rather have been the one who took the bullet, you understand? Operation Daggerfall really did change the course of history. I know. I was there. What they praise and trumpet is partly true. But what they forgot? Too much.
I saw the eyes of a boy, sixteen or so, half burned black, lying still two metres above a pool of blood. What was he thinking before judgment day?

I saw the eyes of a father, half red, half black, fingers trembling as he cradled the body of a Crawler smaller than the rest. Right before Captain Kain called in another barrage. What was he thinking before those deafening blasts?

I saw. Horror... horror and pain, grief and helplessness. Oh, I'd give my whole fortune to forget, you understand? Forget the horror in their eyes, the horror I still feel in my chest, the horror no words can describe. The horror of an empty face hanging above an iron stake.
ep.intro: Empathy is the bridge between one person and another: feeling what someone else is going through, putting yourself where they stand, and understanding at least partly why they do what they do.
ep.effect: Outburst Cast Time reduction and Elemental Damage.
ep.high: you become one with humanity. You understand everyone's circumstances, and everyone's story gets into you. You cry other people's tears and stick your nose into business that isn't yours.
ep.good: therapists, human lie detectors, good alignments.
ep.bad: chaotic alignments, serial killers, non-humanoids.

perks.name: Shared Breath
perks.t1: 2 AP, link with an ally. The next Heart Debuff on either of you is split between you, each at half its duration.
perks.t2: The link lasts the whole combat.

perks.name: Lay Down Arms
perks.t1: 2 AP, a humanoid enemy who can hear you saves against Heart or lowers its weapon for a round.
perks.t2: Up to three enemies at once.

mastered.name: Open Hand
mastered.flavour: You saw the moment they stopped wanting this. So did they.
mastered.text: When an enemy you can see drops to a quarter of its HP or less, offer mercy as a free action: it saves against Heart or stops fighting for the rest of the combat.

combos.name: Cold Read
combos.text: One Analyze action on an NPC reveals what they want most.
combos.deed: Close a case with a confession.

skills.name: Camaraderie
skills.summary: The squad is a world of its own.
skills.quiet: You're not alone in this. You never were.
skills.notices: Kestrel hasn't eaten since the drop. Ask her, not the sergeant.

ep.speaker: Anastasia Vandenberg of Kemizuchi Military Academy
quote: If you don't want to get brainwashed, I'd stay away from that Souji. 'The power of friendship,' then 'the bond of hearts'; he says that stuff without a shred of embarrassment. He wants to befriend everyone he meets and goes around calling people 'comrade' before he's even graduated. Go into a fight with him and before you know it half the enemy team are on our side. Last week he talked that platinum-haired girl from the rival school onto our team, just like that. Is that insane or what? Jealous? Why on earth would I be jealous? Completely ridiculous!
ep.intro: Camaraderie is your teamwork and your solidarity with your squad, plus your knack for making friends and building factions.
ep.effect: Heal/Shield Power; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you become the heart of any team you join. You start seeing the team as its own little world and judge outsiders harder than you mean to.
ep.good: captains, team players.
ep.bad: lone wolves, edgelords, murder hobos.

perks.name: Soulmate
perks.t1: Bond with one teammate and absorb part of the damage they take: 5% at Mastery 1, 10% at Mastery 2, 15% at Mastery 3, 20% at Mastery 4. If they hold Soulmate too, you can tank for each other.
perks.t2: Bond with two teammates.

perks.name: Rally Cry
perks.t1: When an ally drops to 0 HP, every other ally gets +1 AP on their next turn.
perks.t2: +2 AP.

mastered.name: Many Hands
mastered.flavour: Nobody on this squad fights alone. Not even you.
mastered.text: Hand-Off has no limit: give any amount of your AP to any ally within 3 tiles, once per round. An ally you can see may use your reaction as their own.

combos.name: Cultured
combos.text: +1 on Ingenuity and Charisma whenever the talk turns to art, history or holo-dramas: you blend in with anyone who loves them.
combos.deed: Win someone over with a story, a song or a painting.

combos.name: Field Surgeon
combos.text: Field Repair heals living allies as well as machines, and your heals on robotic allies work at full power.
combos.deed: Bring a squadmate back from below 10% HP.

combos.name: Silent Partner
combos.text: An ally next to you shares your stealth.
combos.deed: Get the whole squad through a guarded area unseen.

skills.name: Implication
skills.summary: Metaphor, subtext, poetry and flirting.
skills.quiet: The perfume of corpse-flowers. Someone in this room is rotting.
skills.notices: 'The river was high' means the shipment came early. She's telling you without telling them.

ep.speaker: Aleksandr Donovik Artem of Rigaz Trade Company ADCorp
quote: Jazmine, Jazmine of the dying afternoon, lead the lost soul away from breaking.

Ask ten people in the recon squad and nine won't want to share a transport with me. They say the way I talk isn't easy on the ears. I can rarely sit with someone ten minutes before something about them grates on me, and saying it plainly would be a little... vulgar. So I use metaphor. A faint sweat stain becomes 'the perfume of corpse-flowers in the Sonz marsh.' An uncleaned rifle becomes 'a homemade death at dawn.' I won't hide it: watching them fume without a comeback always brightens my heart a little.

I've lived alone between earth and sky too long for one or two more haters to matter. But Jazmine is something else. Coarse as an old man from Chezknov, and yet sometimes... gentle as a golden lotus in a stinking marsh. Can your smile melt my heart? Hard to say. The one thing I know for certain: you make me want to be a better man.
ep.intro: Implication is your command of metaphor. You catch people's meaning when they talk in figures, you understand difficult poetry and literature, and it helps a great deal with lying and with flirting. (With literature. It can't generate a credit card.)
ep.effect: Heart Debuff DS bonus; unlocks metaphor options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: you drown in the meaning behind every word. Every metaphor lands, but you fall into the "yes means no, no means yes" trap.
ep.good: poets, writers, artists, the hopelessly lovestruck.
ep.bad: the antisocial, blunt people, paladins.

perks.name: Sweet Talker
perks.t1: Once you've charmed or flattered someone this scene (a Charisma or Implication success), buffing them or debuffing them gives you +2 AP. If someone you charmed debuffs you, −2 AP: betrayal stings.
perks.t2: +3 AP, and the sting is gone.

perks.name: Double Meaning
perks.t1: Say one sentence that means one thing to the enemy and another to your squad. The squad gets +2 on the action it hinted at.
perks.t2: The enemy acts on the false meaning.

mastered.name: Their Own Idea
mastered.flavour: You never told them. You just let them get there.
mastered.text: Once per scene, hide a suggestion inside a sentence. The listener believes it was their own idea and acts on it, unless it would harm them directly.

combos.name: Verse of War
combos.text: Outbursts cast while you speak in verse get +1 tile of range and +10% damage.
combos.deed: Cast an Outburst that ends a fight, and say something worth remembering while you do it.

skills.name: Will Power
skills.summary: The strength of the soul, and of its link to its twin in the upper realm. Attack skill for Soul spells that strike.
skills.quiet: Breathe deep. Meditate until the doubt falls away.
skills.notices: The air here is thick. The heart can draw deep, but slowly.

ep.speaker: Nora the "Witch" of Arkvelton
quote: Yes, your heart can shatter like silken tofu. Connecting to the twin world is no joke. Pulling a few little sparks over ten minutes, anyone with a cheap Emanator can do that. A bolt over ten thousand volts in two seconds? Try it and you'll learn what a Mana Short is. There was a Linker once who didn't just bleed internally; he shorted so hard his heart burst on the spot and left a hole in his chest. Outburst craft needs a pure heart, the strength to resist temptation, and the understanding to hold the connection. Now breathe deep and meditate until your doubts fall away!
ep.intro: Will Power is the strength of your heart: generosity and spiritual sharpness. A person's soul lives in the heart, and Will Power measures both your mental strength and the strength of the soul inside you. Essential for Outbursts and Emanators.
ep.effect: Outburst Damage and Mana Syphon; gates heart-based equipment.
ep.high: your heart and soul turn hard and strong. You connect easily with the supernatural, but you slip easily into delusion, because the link to your upper-realm soul is so strong you can't tell this world from that one.
ep.good: Emanator users, monks, crusaders, Bonders.
ep.bad: Evoker users, scientists, melee users.

perks.name: Heart Overload
perks.t1: Pay for an Outburst with HP instead of mana, at 2 HP per point of mana.
perks.t2: 1 HP per point.

perks.name: Resonance
perks.t1: When an ally casts an Outburst within 3 tiles of you, your next Outburst costs 20% less mana.
perks.t2: 40% less.

mastered.name: The Twin Pays
mastered.flavour: Up there, someone with your face flinches. Down here, the spell lands.
mastered.text: Once per combat, cast a Soul spell with no mana and no Strain: your twin in the upper realm pays for it.

combos.name: Verse of War
combos.text: Outbursts cast while you speak in verse get +1 tile of range and +10% damage.
combos.deed: Cast an Outburst that ends a fight, and say something worth remembering while you do it.

combos.name: Twin Souls
combos.text: Once per session, ask your twin soul in the upper realm one question. Your mid-level Outbursts can draw on a third school.
combos.deed: Survive a Mana Short.

skills.name: Lore Master
skills.summary: The occultist's library. Mirrors Rumination.
skills.quiet: Mother wanted to know. So do you.
skills.notices: That mark is a Lumeri saint's seal, but upside down. It's a warning, not a blessing.

ep.speaker: Andrade Lovelace, "Mother" of the Institute of Forgotten Knowledge
quote: Mother lived to hear every story from a thousand worlds. It was a small dream from when I was young and foolish, a spark struck the moment I walked into the modest little library my father kept in secret. It grew into a roaring fire in my heart: a hunger to touch every stream of knowledge that science calls baseless. The marches of the half-horse Zarkast tribe. Tales of wicked witches in the woods outside Albert Town. Rumours of magic gates that transform those who pass. Love stories between humans and beings of the upper realm.
Mother wanted to know, to understand, to hold the chance to prove it true. And after more than a hundred years of study, they chose Mother for this seat. The one who makes the unreal real.
ep.intro: Lore Master is how well you adapt to and absorb supernatural knowledge, the kind science dismisses as baseless. You understand how it works without leaning on dangerous shortcuts like charms or spiritual links.
ep.effect: Outburst Range bonus; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you can tell at once whether something is the work of the supernatural and how to deal with it. Comfortable among mages, but you start rejecting proven science because you see the supernatural threads behind it.
ep.good: dreamers, divine casters, spellswords.
ep.bad: scientists, hackers, barbarians.

perks.name: Old Tongue
perks.t1: Read any ancient or upper-realm script.
perks.t2: Speak it; any upper-realm being will parley with you once.

perks.name: Rite in the Field
perks.t1: Wards and rituals cost 1 AP less in combat.
perks.t2: 2 AP less.

mastered.name: True Name
mastered.flavour: You know what it's called. It knows you know.
mastered.text: Once per session, name an upper-realm being, curse or creature you've studied. For the rest of the scene it takes +50% damage from you and your allies, and it can't lie to you.

combos.name: Cultured
combos.text: +1 on Ingenuity and Charisma whenever the talk turns to art, history or holo-dramas: you blend in with anyone who loves them.
combos.deed: Win someone over with a story, a song or a painting.

combos.name: Twin Souls
combos.text: Once per session, ask your twin soul in the upper realm one question. Your mid-level Outbursts can draw on a third school.
combos.deed: Survive a Mana Short.

skills.name: Composure
skills.summary: A face that never moves.
skills.quiet: Stand still. Then stand stiller.
skills.notices: His eyes slipped off yours. That was the moment. He's done.

ep.speaker: Kaizer Meyer Reinch Wolf of Central Command Center
quote: In the ring, kid, the first punch you throw doesn't come from your fist. What you need is your eyes! When he walks at you, arms up and chest out, you stand still. When your lips feel his boozy breath, you stand still. When his bloodthirsty stare locks on yours, you stand stiller. Only when his eyes slip off yours do you get to move. The only problem is, the fight ended long before that.
ep.intro: Composure is your ability to stay calm in any situation. Neither a monster at midnight nor the woman waiting at the end of the alley can move your face an inch.
ep.effect: Heart Debuff save roll; unlocks calm options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: your face goes stone in every situation. Great when someone threatens or interrogates you; terrible for anyone who just wants to be friendly.
ep.good: security guards, police, iron men, lead men.
ep.bad: small bois, shy bois, studs and sluts.

perks.name: You Get Used to It
perks.t1: −1 AP when an ally takes a Brain Debuff; +3 AP when you heal or shield an ally against one.
perks.t2: No penalty.

perks.name: Flat Line
perks.t1: When combat starts, pick one enemy. Your calm unnerves it: −1 to its attacks while it can see you.

mastered.name: Still Water
mastered.flavour: Nothing goes in. Nothing comes out.
mastered.text: You're immune to Brain Debuffs, and nothing reads you: not your intent, your lies or your HP, not even Analyze or Empathy.

combos.name: Between Heartbeats
combos.text: Once per combat, when an enemy starts an action in your sight, take a 2 AP action first.
combos.deed: Come through an ambush without being hit.

combos.name: The Voice
combos.text: Once per session, give an order in combat; enemy rank-and-file who fail a Heart save obey it for one action.
combos.deed: Stare down an enemy officer until they back off.

skills.name: Faith
skills.summary: The saints judge. You deliver.
skills.quiet: Only the saints may judge. You only deliver.
skills.notices: The pilgrims keep the left aisle clear. Someone important is coming.

ep.speaker: Sister October of the Lumeri Church
quote: Holy Father Nerukhan taught that the love between people is everlasting. The world above where He reigns is no different from the world of men. But as a keeper of the saint's faith, I cannot sit idle before their contemptible deeds one more day.
Only the saints may judge and carry out justice. But delivering the sinners into their hands? That is our job.
*racks shotgun*
*heavy metal plays*
ep.intro: Faith is your ability to place your trust in higher powers. In a world where anything can happen, plenty of people face life's cruelty on the strength of belief. And unlike real life, here the odds of a prayer coming true are better than 1%.
ep.effect: Blessing Power and Blessing cooldown reduction; gates devotional equipment.
ep.high: your bond with your faith tightens and amplifies everything your religion gives you. Everyone else sees an insufferable zealot, or worse, a heretic.
ep.good: crusaders, divine classes, cultists, missionaries.
ep.bad: atheists, scientists, smartasses.

perks.name: Litany
perks.t1: 2 AP, a spoken prayer: allies within 3 tiles get +1 on saves until your next turn.

perks.name: Holy Ordnance
perks.t1: 3 AP, bless an ally's magazine: it deals +20% damage to upper-realm and cursed beings.
perks.t2: +40%, and two magazines at once.

mastered.name: Judgement Day
mastered.flavour: The saints have looked. They've decided.
mastered.text: Once per combat, 3 AP: judge one enemy you can see. Its next attack against an ally fails, and your attacks against it deal +50% damage until the combat ends.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 3 AP · Once per combat

combos.name: Fire Sermon
combos.text: While you preach (2 AP), your Blessings also leave enemies in range Shaken.
combos.deed: Convert an enemy mid-fight.

skills.name: Conscience
skills.summary: Seeing where an act leads.
skills.quiet: It is not a question of right or left. Only of conscience.
skills.notices: If you take the platinum, the robots stay behind. That is the whole of the choice.

ep.speaker: The Azure Blood Holder
quote: It is not a question of right or wrong. Nor of left or right. In a world of upheaval and chaos, the only thing that makes a God or a Demon is conscience.
ep.intro: Conscience is your ability to tell right from wrong, and to see the good or harm in an act not just now but far into the future, not just for you but for all of humanity.
ep.effect: more Karma earned; unlocks exploration options and Trio-Scale Equipment.
ep.high: you understand the consequences of everything you're about to do. But you think from one angle only, good or evil, right or wrong, and yours is the only one that counts.
ep.good: lawful alignments, living saints, Satan in human skin.
ep.bad: neutral alignments, emotionless robots, weathervanes.

perks.name: Red Line
perks.t1: Name one line you won't cross. While you hold it, +1 on every Heart save.
perks.t2: +2, and allies within 3 tiles get +1.

perks.name: Clean Hands
perks.t1: +2 AP on your next turn after you spare an enemy or protect an innocent.
perks.t2: +3 AP.

mastered.name: Foreseen
mastered.flavour: You saw where it led. This time you take the other road.
mastered.text: Once per session, after a major decision goes wrong, rewind to just before it. The Narrator tells you what would have happened, and you choose again.

combos.name: What Could Be
combos.text: Once per session, before a major decision, the Narrator shows you a brief vision of the best outcome within reach, and one way to get there.
combos.deed: Talk someone out of a terrible choice by showing them where it leads.

skills.name: Authority
skills.summary: The measure of cool, and your Leadership rating.
skills.quiet: They'll fall in line. They always do.
skills.notices: The guards are watching you, not him. You could just tell them to stand aside.

ep.speaker: Brengan Springfield, the "Juggernaut" of the 101st Hellraiser Division
quote: I don't need to tell you about Hank Ladan's war record, kid. Everything you need, you'll get from watching how people treat him.

A skinny frame in a plain, no-frills uniform. Easy stance, warm laugh. Nobody would guess Hank Ladan outranks a marshal, and nobody dares look him in the eye, or at the five stars on his shoulder. Not even a guy like me who won three straight wrestling tournaments in the Marine mess hall. Something comes off him that makes your knees want to buckle, out of respect or fear. He has the nepo babies over in the Air branch falling in line, and every agent in the enforcement bureau bows when he passes. A busted-up marine like me? Honestly, I'd rather hunt ten Ork fangs in one afternoon than hear one word of criticism from him.
ep.intro: Authority is the measure of cool. Anyone can put on a suit; Authority decides whether you look cool in it. Be the groomsman and still draw more of the bride's eyes and respect than the groom. Oh, so dignified.
ep.effect: more Reputation earned; unlocks dominance options in exploration and dialogue.
ep.high: people mistake you for a general, a leader or a top CEO, which raises the odds you get investigated and make the news for buying apples at the market instead of the supermarket.
ep.good: soldiers, police, security, teachers, anyone who has to be cool.
ep.bad: sugar babies, fuckboys (you risk ending up married instead of a one-night stand).

perks.name: Outclassed
perks.t1: +3 AP if your squad gets the first kill and you helped damage that target; −2 AP if your squad takes the first casualty.
perks.t2: No penalty, and whoever made the kill also gets +1 AP.

perks.name: Real Power
perks.t1: In any organisation, you can tell who actually holds the power, whatever the titles say.
perks.t2: And that person agrees to see you.

mastered.name: On My Mark
mastered.flavour: You say go. They're already gone.
mastered.text: Once per round, 1 AP: order an ally who can hear you. They take one action right away, outside their turn, paying with their own AP.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 1 AP · Once per round

combos.name: The Voice
combos.text: Once per session, give an order in combat; enemy rank-and-file who fail a Heart save obey it for one action.
combos.deed: Stare down an enemy officer until they back off.

attrs.name: Intelligence
attrs.fx: Sigil words per spell and Sigil damage

attrs.name: Expression
attrs.fx: Sigil AP cost and elemental damage

attrs.name: Insight
attrs.fx: Healing given and Soul spell cost

classesFull.name: Marksman
classesFull.moveText: Aimed shots add no Heat. Once per turn, a Burst costs 2 AP instead of 3. With a bow, an Aimed shot gets +3 to hit instead of +2.

classesFull.name: Fighter
classesFull.moveText: Spend 1 Momentum: move up to 2 tiles as part of a melee attack. This movement provokes no opportunity attacks.

classesFull.name: Defender
classesFull.moveText: Gain Guard equal to 1 + your Durability modifier (max 5) and become Braced (+2 Defense) until you move. Interpose is available whenever you hold Guard.

classesFull.name: Medic
classesFull.moveText: Heal an adjacent ally 20 x your Healing given multiplier and end their Bleeding. Costs no Supplies. You stabilise a Downed ally for 1 AP.

classesFull.name: Assassin
classesFull.moveText: Mark an enemy you can see: it becomes Marked (your squad gets +1 to hit it; it can't become Hidden).

classesFull.name: Mage
classesFull.moveText: Damage words (FIRE, SHOCK, FREEZE) cost 1 charge less each. A spell still costs at least 1.

classesFull.name: Warden
classesFull.moveText: You can Evoke a lone STAY glyph with no Subject as a cover rune, from a tile next to it: full cover on its tile and one tile next to it for 2 rounds + your Sigil duration bonus.

classesFull.name: Scribe
classesFull.moveText: Spend 1 charge: an ally within 6 tiles gets +1 AP on their next turn (AP ceiling applies). On the area map the +1 lands on this overworld round's AP.

classesFull.name: Trickster
classesFull.moveText: The BIND word costs 1 charge less, and its Body save is against 14 + your debuff strength instead of 12.

classesFull.name: Channeler
classesFull.moveText: The first Damage-school spell you cast each turn adds no Strain.

classesFull.name: Guardian
classesFull.moveText: A Buff-school cast (Soul cast AP, 20 MP base): an ally in range gains a shield of 30 x your Healing given multiplier until the end of combat.

classesFull.name: Bard
classesFull.moveText: Spend 10 MP: an ally within 6 tiles gets +2 on their next roll. Adds no Strain.

classesFull.name: Hexer
classesFull.moveText: Status-school spells that inflict Fear cost 5 MP less, and Fear you inflict lasts 1 extra round.

families.name: Frontline
families.blurb: Hold the line, or break theirs.

families.name: Guns and hunters
families.blurb: Range, patience and a lot of brass.

families.name: Sigil casters
families.blurb: Mind magic: command words drawn through an Evoker.

families.name: Soul and faith
families.blurb: Heart magic, prayer and the things that answer.

families.name: Voices and leaders
families.blurb: Words as weapons, people as armies.

families.name: Hybrids and wanderers
families.blurb: Two trades at once, or a little of everything.

families.name: All-in
families.blurb: Everything in one place: all 6 Core points in one Core, a skill at 7, and nothing else. A 7/1/1 character.

items.name: Bulwark
items.blurb: Stands in the doorway so nobody else has to. Has been shot more times than most people have been hugged.

items.name: Bodyguard
items.blurb: Sees the knife before the client does, and gets between them. Paid by the day, loyal past it.

items.name: Brawler
items.blurb: Fixes problems with fists and leaves the paperwork to people with smaller hands.

items.name: Berserker
items.blurb: Doesn't feel the wound until the fight is over, and doesn't stop until somebody makes it over.

items.name: Fencer
items.blurb: Blade or pistol, the same rule: be somewhere else when they swing.

items.name: Monk
items.blurb: Trained until the body and the breath became one weapon. Calm right up to the point of impact.

items.name: Sharpshooter
items.blurb: Identify. Squeeze. Breathe. Patient as stone, and the last thing a lot of people never saw.

items.name: Heavy Gunner
items.blurb: Carries the gun nobody else can lift and believes volume of fire is a personality.

items.name: Ranger
items.blurb: Reads tracks, wind and silence. Knows where the enemy is before the map does.

items.name: Grenadier
items.blurb: Every problem is a load-bearing wall, and every wall has a weak spot.

items.name: Infiltrator
items.blurb: In and out before the guard finishes yawning. Nobody remembers seeing them, which is the point.

items.name: Stalker
items.blurb: Waits in the dark for the right moment, then becomes the reason people fear the dark.

items.name: Thief
items.blurb: Light fingers, quick hands, and a professional respect for good locks.

items.name: Spy
items.blurb: Smiles, lies and never sweats. Has had four names this year and liked two of them.

items.name: Sigilist
items.blurb: Draws FIRE · SEEK · SPREAD faster than most people draw breath. Smells faintly of scorched Evoker.

items.name: Sentinel
items.blurb: Raises walls of command words around the squad, and lectures them about it afterwards.

items.name: Enchanter
items.blurb: Inscribes the squad's gear before the fight, so the fight is shorter than it should be.

items.name: Jinx
items.blurb: Finds the weakness, names it, and makes it worse. Enemies blind, slow and confused, in that order.

items.name: Detective
items.blurb: First: no casings. Second: the wall is dented from the far side. Third: you're lying.

items.name: Engineer
items.blurb: Keeps the guns firing, the doors opening and the robots alive. Talks to machines more than people.

items.name: Scholar
items.blurb: Has read about it. Has read about everything. Will tell you, at length, in the middle of the firefight.

items.name: Stormcaller
items.blurb: Imagines the lightning so hard the world gives it to them. Heart pounding, hands smoking.

items.name: Mender
items.blurb: Feels your wound from across the room and closes it before you finish screaming.

items.name: Confessor
items.blurb: Hears the squad's sins, prays over their wounds, and reports to nobody but the saints.

items.name: Zealot
items.blurb: Only the saints may judge. The zealot delivers. Usually with a shotgun.

items.name: Witch
items.blurb: Knows the old stories are true and the twin world is listening. Respected, feared, never invited twice.

items.name: Harbinger
items.blurb: Speaks in omens. Enemies hear their own worst fear in every word, and run from it.

items.name: Silver Tongue
items.blurb: Can talk anyone into anything, and has talked several people into regretting it.

items.name: Troubadour
items.blurb: Turns a squad into a chorus. Morale goes up, enemy morale goes elsewhere.

items.name: Captain
items.blurb: Doesn't raise their voice. Doesn't need to. People simply do what they say.

items.name: Enforcer
items.blurb: Every conversation ends with the other side agreeing. How it gets there is up to them.

items.name: Spellblade
items.blurb: Draws Sigils with the sword tip. Three slashes, then a storm opens in the enemy's head.

items.name: Crusader
items.blurb: Strong arm, certain heart. Walks into the dark first and says a word for those who don't walk out.

items.name: Witch Hunter
items.blurb: Knows what the shadow is, and what kind of round it needs.

items.name: Field Medic
items.blurb: Under fire, on their knees, hands in someone's chest, telling them a terrible joke. Never leaves anyone behind.

items.name: Survivor
items.blurb: Lived where nothing lives. Throws first, ducks second, eats whatever's left.

items.name: Drifter
items.blurb: A little of everything and no home in any of it. Never quite who the room expects.

items.name: Living Wall
items.blurb: Doesn't dodge. Doesn't need to.

items.name: Wrecking Ball
items.blurb: One swing settles the argument, and the wall behind it.

items.name: Deadeye
items.blurb: Never the second shot.

items.name: Phantom
items.blurb: Was in the room the whole time. Nobody remembers letting them in.

items.name: Savant
items.blurb: Draws a Sigil before the rest of the room finishes the word.

items.name: Illusionist
items.blurb: Pictures the fire so clearly the Evoker can't tell it's not there yet.

items.name: Heartreader
items.blurb: Hears what you meant, not what you said, and answers that.

items.name: Unbroken
items.blurb: The heart holds. Everything in front of it doesn't.

items.name: Prophet
items.blurb: Their patron answers on the first ring.

origins.name: Central City
origins.Home: Earth, the capital of the old centre.
origins.Upbringing: precincts, bank cards, shock batons, somebody else doing the dirty work.
origins.You know: city services, officials, the precincts, the inner ring's gossip, how to get anything done with paperwork.
origins.People see you as: soft, rich, connected, out of place past the walls.
origins.Traits that fit: Central City Kid, Inner Ring Heir, Slicer, Wanted, Machine-Faced, Right of Way.
origins.Hook: a family account someone at the CCEC is watching.

origins.name: The Thousand-Planet frontier
origins.Home: an extraction world, outpost or mining moon of the Thousand-Planet City.
origins.Upbringing: quotas, shift sirens, robots doing the jobs nobody survives.
origins.You know: mining, logistics, outpost life, the Thousand World Legion's ranks and rackets.
origins.People see you as: hard-working, expendable, owned by the quota.
origins.Traits that fit: Glass Runner, Heavyworlder, Symbol of Order, Field Medic, Moon Hunter.
origins.Hook: the foreman who still owes you a shift's pay.

origins.name: Hellraiser camps
origins.Home: the barracks worlds and mess halls behind the Hellraiser front.
origins.Upbringing: a soldier's child, or a soldier from sixteen. Orks were the bedtime story, and then the job.
origins.You know: Hellraiser doctrine, Orks, weapons, field rations, which officers get people killed.
origins.People see you as: brave, loud, disposable, a thug to the polite.
origins.Traits that fit: Forlorn Hope, Spray and Pray, Grenadier's Arm, Live to Fight Another Day, Squad Anchor.
origins.Hook: a sergeant who'd take you back, and a deserter who wants you to say nothing.

origins.name: Lumeri cloisters
origins.Home: a cloister or pilgrim world of the Lumeri Church.
origins.Upbringing: rites, scripture, the saints' feast days, nuns who could field-strip a shotgun.
origins.You know: the Church, its saints and Holy Father Nerukhan, its rites, its politics, its charity.
origins.People see you as: devout, trustworthy, judgemental, the Church's eyes.
origins.Traits that fit: Mind Without Fog, True Believer, Heretic, Pacifist.
origins.Hook: the abbess who expects a report.

origins.name: The Adamantile Brigade
origins.Home: a fortress-house of the knightly order.
origins.Upbringing: squire to a knight who slept in snake pits and arm-wrestled concrete for fun.
origins.You know: the Brigade's oaths and feuds, heavy arms, endurance, the Church's ceremonies.
origins.Traits that fit: Sworn Sibling, Pain Eater, Squad Anchor.
origins.Hook: the knight you squired for, still alive, still asking for help with breakfast.

origins.name: Kemizuchi, or the school across town
origins.Home: the officer academy, or its rival.
origins.Upbringing: drills, rankings, rivalries, friendship speeches nobody was embarrassed by.
origins.You know: officers, tactics, the old-boy network, the rival school's secrets (or yours).
origins.Traits that fit: Blade Recluse, Drill Echo, Rival, Born Officer.
origins.Hook: your classmate, now outranking you. (Suggested: the rival school quietly takes mixed families' children.)

origins.name: Arkvelton
origins.Upbringing: breathing exercises, meditation, the heart's link to the twin world, friends who shorted out.
origins.You know: Soul magic, Emanators, Mana Shorts, witch lore, the stories outside Albert Town.
origins.People see you as: a witch, gifted, dangerous, faintly heretical.
origins.Hook: the teacher who told you never to come back without the thing you took.

origins.name: The southern sects
origins.Home: the martial sects of the south.
origins.Upbringing: forms, katas and Sigils drawn with fists and blades. Professor Avdol sneers at people like you.
origins.You know: martial arts, the sects' lineages and feuds, Blade Scribe lore.
origins.Hook: a sect elder who wants a scroll back.

origins.name: The scholar halls
origins.Home: the Science Team's labs, a university, or the Institute of Forgotten Knowledge.
origins.Upbringing: libraries, lectures, Evokers, or banned books.
origins.You know: Sigil theory, history, science (or the occult), who's publishing what.
origins.People see you as: clever, useless in a fight, insufferable.
origins.Traits that fit: Sigil Savant, Occultist, Bottle Butts for Eyes, Cold Case.
origins.Hook: a research partner who credited themselves for your work.

origins.name: Mandestra and the trade lanes
origins.Home: a merchant house, a market stall, or a Rigaz Trade Company posting.
origins.Upbringing: haggling, ledgers, armed caravans, contracts with small print.
origins.You know: prices, routes, merchants, the RTC, who's smuggling what.
origins.Traits that fit: Market Blood, Company Man, Cover Story, Lunarshine.
origins.Hook: a creditor, and a shipment that never arrived.

origins.name: The gold-coin frontier
origins.Home: a frontier town past Central City's reach, where gold coins are money and the Smetanita Conjunction is the law.
origins.Upbringing: saloons, debts, favours, the Papa's people on every corner.
origins.You know: the black market, crime families, smuggling, frontier law.
origins.Traits that fit: Gambler, Wanted, Cover Story, Rogue Element.
origins.Hook: a favour you owe the Conjunction.

origins.name: The lowlands
origins.Home: Earth's ruined lowlands past the desert: Black Scavenger country, a forest of dead buildings.
origins.You know: ruins, scavenging, traps, survival, the Black Scavengers.
origins.Hook: the scavenger crew that thinks you're dead.

origins.name: Bazaim
origins.Home: the human nation that made peace with Daggerfall's survivors.
origins.Upbringing: neighbours with abilities, families mixed by love, Central City's spies everywhere.
origins.You know: espers, the truth about Crawlers (you've seen them as people), Bazaim's politics, how the CCEC operates.
origins.People see you as (in Central City): a spy, a traitor, a monster-lover.
origins.Traits that fit: Crawler-Blooded (needs a review against the one-way curse), Cover Story, Heaven's Faithful.
origins.Hook: someone in your family is a Crawler, and you can see them.

origins.name: The Ork borderlands
origins.Home: the frontier where human towns sit next to Ork warbands.
origins.Upbringing: raids, truces, trading with the enemy, maybe raised by them.
origins.You know: Orks, their warbands and parley, border survival.
origins.People see you as: half-savage, a traitor to some, a guide to others.
origins.Traits that fit: Raised by Orks, Beast Handler, Moon Hunter.
origins.Hook: the warband that wants you home.

traits.name: Mind Without Fog
traits.flavour: You were raised in a Lumeri cloister, or by priests of some other faith. Whatever you believe now, your mind is still water. Nobody has ever managed to stir it.
up: Still Water: gain 2 Core points at creation, to raise any Core above what your skills need. Heart Debuffs never affect you.
down: Unmoving: gear bonuses to Attributes and Skills don't work on you, and your Karma can never change.

traits.name: The Brightest Light
traits.flavour: Burn it down, all of it. The brightest light burns out the fastest, and you've never cared how long you last.
up: Blaze: each kill this combat gives +10% damage, up to +50%.
down: Burnout: weapons wear twice as fast in your hands, and when the fighting stops you crash: −2 on every roll until you rest.

traits.name: Southern Fist
traits.flavour: You trained with the southern sects, where martial arts and magic were never separated. Your fists are weapons. Anything else in your hands is a clumsy stick.
up: These Hands: while fighting with nothing but gloves, +1 AP per turn and +20% Physical Damage.
down: Not That: every attack with any other weapon, guns included, costs +1 AP.

traits.name: Forlorn Hope
traits.flavour: The Hellraiser storm units go in first and come back last, if they come back at all. You volunteered, and you'd volunteer again.
up: Charge: +2 AP on any turn you end closer to an enemy than you started.
down: No Way Back: no armour above Class I, and you can never take the Retreat or Disengage action.

traits.name: Grenadier's Arm
traits.flavour: In the mess halls they arm-wrestle. In the field you throw: grenades, crates, Orks, the occasional squadmate.
up: Long Throw: +2 throwing range. You can throw anything under your carry weight, allies and enemies included; damage scales with its weight.
down: Strained Arm: thrown weapons cost +1 AP.

traits.name: Glass Runner
traits.flavour: You were born on a low-gravity mining moon, and your bones never set right in real gravity. So you learned to move before anything could break them.
up: Runner: +5 Initiative, and your first move each combat costs 1 AP less.
down: Glass: +50% limb damage taken. A broken leg halves your Movement until it's set.

traits.name: Blade Recluse
traits.flavour: While your cohort at the academy drank and courted, you trained alone with one blade. Now the world is ending, and suddenly everyone wants to know you.
up: One Blade: weapon mastery levels 25% faster. Name one weapon: it can't be disarmed and gets one extra mod slot.
